title: Fractional-chunk acknowledgement and priority-aware reconnect for SSE streams
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: Current SSE reconnect semantics replay whole chunks when a client loses connection and reconnects. For long-lived streaming responses (large JSONL structured outputs, function-call frames, or multimedia-like deltas) this causes either duplicated partial outputs on client-side or the server re-sends large ranges, increasing load and latency. We also need a way to prioritize reconnections from high-importance clients (reserved capacity / enterprise) without destabilizing default replay behavior.

Goal: Implement a fractional-chunk acknowledgement (FCA) mechanism plus a lightweight priority-aware reconnect handshake so clients and servers can: 1) acknowledge sub-chunk progress (byte-offset or token-offset), 2) request prioritized replay windows, and 3) negotiate minimal backfills while preserving idempotence for function-call/tool frames and structured JSON outputs. The solution must be backward compatible with existing SSE and our resume-token flow and must interoperate safely with function-calling markers and JSONL chunk boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes optional FCA headers and resume tokens that include sub-chunk offsets; existing clients without FCA continue to work unchanged.
Clients can submit a reconnect request with desired priority level; server honors priority within configured rate limits and capacity tiers.

Replayed fragments preserve function-call atomicity: tool call frames are never split by fractional replays; server upgrades partially-acknowledged fragments to complete, or replies with a guarded abort marker if impossible.
Regression tests added: simulated mid-chunk disconnects for large JSONL outputs, verifying no duplicate function-call side effects and correct client-visible ordering.
Observable metrics: fractional-ack rate, average backfill bytes per reconnect, priority-replay latency; dashboards updated in Console release runtime-1.25.
A staged rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to whole-chunk replay if checksum mismatch or backward-client detected.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Evelyn Chen: Initial spike found that using token offsets is more robust than raw byte offsets across quantized/whitespace-normalized pipelines. Drafted protocol sketch and handshake extensions.

2026-02-20 - Marco Rivera: Implemented prototype on staging: server keeps per-session fragment index map with {fragment_id, seq, token_start, token_end, checksum}. FCA ACKs update token_end. Observed memory growth under pathological livetext workloads; need LRU tombstone for old fragments.
2026-02-25 - Design review (Kiran Patel): Confirmed UX for clients — expose resume_token and resume_offset fields in client SDKs; UX will show a subtle 'partial replay' indicator in Console logs.

2026-03-01 - Security (Aisha Patel): Reviewed for attack surface: priority field cannot be client-supplied at high values without an auth scope. Added requirement to validate prioritized reconnects against account tier and rate limits.

2026-03-04 - Marco Rivera: Edge case found: fractional ACKs on compressed token streams (quantized 4-bit) require server to maintain uncompressed token mapping or store checkpoints at compression boundaries. Opted for checkpointing every N tokens to limit overhead.

2026-03-07 - QA (Liam O'Neill): Ran long-tail reconnect fuzzing for function-call sequences. Two failure modes: 1) partial function-call frame acknowledged then replayed truncated causing client JSON parser error; 2) duplicate side-effects when server re-executes tool calls. Proposed server-side deterministic rehydration: server records tool-call IDs and re-sends idempotency hints in replay frames.

2026-03-08 - Marco Rivera: Merging RFC to main branch (WIP). Next: implement tombstone GC, integrate priority auth checks, create migration guide for SDKs. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862 (draft).
implementation_notes: Key components: 1) Resume token expansion: resume_token => {epoch, fragment_seq, fragment_id, fragment_checksum, resume_offset}. Represented in URL-safe base64. 2) FCA ACK: client sends periodic 'X-Redwood-FCA: fragment_id:token_offset' (or via /ack endpoint for non-streamable clients). 3) Priority handshake: on reconnect, client includes 'X-Redwood-Priority: low|standard|high' and auth scope; server uses policy to decide immediate replay vs queued backfill. 4) Function-call safety: server will coalesce fractional fragments that contain function-call start markers and only emit replay boundaries at safe semantically-aligned points; otherwise it requests a repair flush from model pipeline. 5) Backward compatibility: if server sees legacy resume tokens, falls back to existing resume window semantics.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: enable FCA on internal staging with 10 internal customers and internal SDKs. 2) Open beta: opt-in via account flag for selected customers, monitor metrics for memory and backfill bytes. 3) Gradual enable: 25% -> 100% for reserved capacity tenants; include console feature flag to toggle forced whole-chunk fallback. 4) SDK release: Node/Python clients add transparent resume_offset handling and expose explicit ack() helpers. 5) Monitor: dashboards for fractional_ack_ratio, prioritized_replay_latency, idempotent_tool_replays.
risks_and_mitigations: Memory growth from fragment index: mitigation - implement LRU tombstone and size-based GC; tombstones stored for minimal TTL aligned with resume window.
Client misbehavior manipulating priority: mitigation - server validates JWT scopes and enforces account-level quotas and rate limiting.

Function-call duplication: mitigation - server stores compact idempotency markers for tool calls for the session and includes 'tool-id' in replay frames; clients must honor tool-id to dedupe side effects.
Compression boundary mismatch: mitigation - checkpoint uncompressed token offsets every 1024 tokens; configurable per-account for low-latency customers.
Interoperability with older clients: mitigation - explicit version negotiation; if client sends 'X-Redwood-FCA: v1' but server unknown, fallback to whole-chunk semantics.
